## Lee — going halves on a dumper

I reckon it’s worth us buying a secondhand tracked dumper between us rather than paying to hire one every time we’ve got a bigger job. We’ve worked together long enough to know it’ll get used, and looking at this year’s figures, it’s not far off costing us the same to hire as it would to buy.

### The sums

We hired the tracked dumper from Sittingbourne for 14 days this year at £85 a day. That’s £1,190 before the £30 delivery charge each time, and roughly £1,600 all in over the year.

There’s a bloke in Faversham selling a 2019 500kg tracked dumper for £1,650 ono. He says it had new tracks last spring. At the asking price, that’s **£825 each**, possibly less if there’s a deal to be done.

At this year’s use, the purchase price is about a year’s hire money. Even if we only use it half as much, it’s about two years. That’s before servicing and repairs, obviously, so we need to have a proper look rather than take his word for everything.

### It’s not just the hire bill

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring. Having our own means it’s there when we need it, without waiting for availability or a delivery driver turning up at 11 and losing us half the morning.

And neither of us wants another Hernhill. Barrowing six ton of muck because the hire place hadn’t got one added two days to the job, and your back was gone for a week afterwards.

### How we’d sort it

We’d own it half each and keep it under cover in my lean-to at the yard. Servicing and normal wear-and-tear repairs would be split 50/50, fuel paid by whoever’s using it, and whoever breaks it through misuse pays for that repair. We’d agree bookings between us so there’s no messing about.

If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it on. They seem to hold their value, though there’s no guarantee we’d get every penny back.

**Come and have a look with me this Saturday.** No commitment until we’ve checked it over, but worth seeing it before someone else has it.
